checks_performed: Read only the authorized source input and revision draft and compared the exact target against the proposed construction and conclusion.
Reconstructed G exactly as K9 minus the seven cyclic pairs vi vi+1 and independently checked all structural arguments.
Ran the persisted exact-arithmetic checker over every relevant vertex subset, all 14 H-edges, all local incidence/color configurations, and all 3^7 incidence-type assignments.

Directly encoded the no-monochromatic-triangle condition as an exact 29-variable Boolean CNF over all 42 triangles. A complete DPLL search with pq fixed red proved it unsatisfiable; fixing pq red is without loss by global color interchange.

claims.claim: Define G on vertices p,q,v0,…,v6 by taking every edge except vi vi+1, with indices modulo 7.
claims.evidence: There are 36 unordered pairs on the nine vertices. Deleting exactly the seven cyclic pairs leaves a well-defined 29-edge finite simple undirected graph. Its induced subgraph H on v0,…,v6 is the complement of C7, while p and q are adjacent to each other and every vi.
claims.search_method: Constructed the complete unordered-pair set exactly and compared its complement in E(G) with the seven prescribed cyclic pairs.

claims.claim: The clique number of H is 3.
claims.evidence: A clique of H is an independent set of C7. Any independent set in a 7-cycle has size at most floor(7/2)=3, and {v0,v2,v4} has size three. Exact enumeration of all 128 vertex subsets also returned omega(H)=3.
claims.search_method: Used the complement correspondence and exhaustively tested all subsets of V(H) for pairwise adjacency.

claims.evidence: Every clique uses at most omega(H)=3 vertices from H and at most p and q outside H, so it has size at most five. Exact enumeration independently found omega(G)=5 and rejected every six-vertex subset.
claims.search_method: Derived the clique bound from claim 1 and exhaustively tested all 512 subsets of V(G), including all 84 six-vertex subsets.
claims.witness: The maximum-size clique {p,q,v0,v2,v4} has size five, certifying omega(G)=5<6.

claims.claim: H has no induced cycle of length at least 5.
claims.evidence: Only lengths 5, 6, and 7 are possible. If H[S]=Ck for k≥6, then C7[S] is the complement of Ck and every vertex has degree k−3≥3, impossible in an induced subgraph of C7, whose maximum degree is two. For k=5, the complement is again C5, but a proper induced subgraph of C7 is a disjoint union of paths. Exhaustive testing found no such subset.
claims.search_method: Tested all 29 subsets of H of sizes 5 through 7, recognizing an induced cycle by connectedness and induced degree exactly two at every selected vertex.
claims.witness: The exact exhaustive certificate reports zero induced H-cycles among all candidate subsets of sizes 5, 6, and 7.

claims.claim: G has no induced odd cycle of length at least 5.
claims.evidence: In an induced cycle of length k≥5, every selected vertex has induced degree two. Either universal vertex p or q would instead have induced degree k−1, so neither can occur. The cycle would therefore lie in H, where claim 3 excludes it. Exact enumeration of all candidate subsets of odd sizes 5, 7, and 9 found none.
claims.search_method: Applied the universal-vertex reduction and exhaustively checked all 163 subsets of G having relevant odd cardinality.
claims.witness: The exact exhaustive certificate reports zero induced odd G-cycles of lengths 5, 7, or 9.

claims.claim: The independence number of H is 2.
claims.evidence: An independent set of H is a clique of C7. The cycle is triangle-free but has edges, so its clique number, and hence alpha(H), is exactly two. Exact subset enumeration agrees.
claims.search_method: Used complementation and exhaustively tested all 128 subsets of H for independence.
claims.witness: {v0,v1} is an independent pair in H, while no independent triple exists.

claims.claim: Every edge of H belongs to a triangle of H.
claims.evidence: After rotating and reversing indices, every H-edge is vi vi+2 or vi vi+3. In the first case vi+4 is adjacent in H to both endpoints; in the second case vi+5 is adjacent to both. The checker enumerated all 14 H-edges and found at least one common H-neighbor for each.
claims.search_method: Enumerated every H-edge and its common-neighbor set, while separately checking the modular extension formula.
claims.witness: Triangle extensions are vi vi+2 vi+4 and vi vi+3 vi+5, with indices modulo 7.

claims.claim: After fixing pq red in a coloring without monochromatic triangles, V(H) partitions into three incidence types A=(blue,blue), B=(red,blue), and C=(blue,red).
claims.evidence: Global color interchange permits pq to be assumed red. For every v, the pair (pv,qv) cannot be (red,red), since pqv would be a red triangle. The other three pairs are exhaustive and mutually exclusive, so they partition V(H).
claims.search_method: Exhausted all four possible ordered color pairs for (pv,qv) with pq fixed red and filtered by the triangle pqv.
claims.witness: The surviving pairs are exactly (blue,blue), (red,blue), and (blue,red).

claims.claim: The type classes B and C are independent in H.
claims.evidence: If adjacent u,v are both in B, their red p-incidences force uv blue to avoid a red triangle puv, while their blue q-incidences force uv red to avoid a blue triangle quv, a contradiction. Interchanging p and q proves the C case. Exhausting both possible colors for uv confirmed no valid local coloring.
claims.search_method: Performed the direct forcing proof and enumerated both colors of a hypothetical B-B or C-C H-edge.
claims.witness: For a B-B edge, pu=pv=red forces uv=blue, whereas qu=qv=blue forces uv=red; the C-C contradiction is symmetric.

claims.claim: The type class A is independent in H.
claims.evidence: For a∈A and an H-neighbor w, at least one of pw,qw is blue by claim 7. Since pa=qa=blue, coloring aw blue would form a blue triangle, so aw is red. If two A-vertices a,a' were adjacent, claim 6 supplies w with aa'w an H-triangle. Each of aa', aw, and a'w is incident with an A-vertex and hence red, producing a red triangle. The checker also exhausted all 24 relevant local configurations.
claims.search_method: Combined the incident-edge forcing argument with every-edge triangle extension, then enumerated three possible types for w and all eight colors of the H-triangle edges.
claims.witness: A hypothetical A-A edge extends to aa'w; the forcing rule makes aa', aw, and a'w all red.

claims.claim: Every red/blue edge-coloring of G contains a monochromatic triangle.
claims.evidence: Assuming otherwise and normalizing pq to red yields the partition A∪B∪C=V(H). Claims 8 and 9 make all three classes independent, while alpha(H)=2 makes their union contain at most six vertices, contradicting |V(H)|=7. Independently, all 2187 type assignments failed, and a direct exact CNF encoding of all 42 graph triangles was proved unsatisfiable by complete DPLL search.
claims.search_method: Used the completed incidence-type proof, exhaustively checked all 3^7 type assignments, and independently ran exact Boolean DPLL on 29 edge-color variables and 85 clauses after fixing pq red by symmetry.
claims.witness: The direct CNF search terminated UNSAT after 327 nodes, 163 branch nodes, 1180 unit propagations, and 164 conflicts.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for one finite simple graph satisfying K6-freeness, odd-hole-freeness, and the two-edge-color triangle Ramsey property. The explicit nine-vertex graph is finite and simple; claims 2, 4, and 10 rigorously establish those three requested properties. This is neither vacuous nor a weaker or mismatched result, and the excluded K4-free follow-up is not asserted. Thus the draft fully resolves the target, and its claimed_resolution of FULL is ACCURATE.
